blocks.text: Technical Evidence Appendix
BMDS2114 warehouse robot navigation

This appendix compiles actual software and measurement evidence for the team to verify. It is not the final academic paper or evidence of individual authorship. It does not replace the team's own critical discussion, contribution records, tutor-approved proposal or required AI-use disclosure.
Measurement scope

The registered ensemble study uses 32 previously inspected development layouts and four existing manual demo presets. Seven controllers each ran the same 36 cases: 252 episodes and 4,092 environment actions. No training, optimizer update or held-out evaluation occurred. The original Phase3 64-case publication and all prior checkpoints remain unchanged.

The ensemble completed 36/36, the same success count as SARSA, DQN and PPO and two more than Q-learning. Its mean successful route length was 17.44 actions versus PPO's 13.08. Its measured local decision cost was 3.90ms versus about 0.86-1.01ms for the four native policies. The evidence does not establish superiority; the ensemble stays optional and the four selected models are not replaced.
How voting is implemented

Each existing RL policy proposes one of Up, Down, Left, Right or Wait from the same public 409-value observation. The most-voted action is executed. Ties use the lowest action index, fixed before measurement. Member history is synchronized to the actual executed action, not each member's own proposal. No fitted voting weights, planner fallback, action mask or hidden event information is used. The ensemble has zero new training actions and no new weight file; its member-set checksum identifies the four original saves.
Figure 1. Development-only ensemble results and local inference cost. Cases were previously inspected; this is not unseen accuracy. Single-run timing includes history handling.

Figure 2. Existing Phase3 development results for the registered unshaped and liveness-feedback candidates. Each family/candidate used 40,000 fresh actions and the same single seed. These are selection outcomes, not held-out claims.
Figure 3. Original Phase2 versus Phase3 checkpoints on the same 64-case product holdout. These are saved results only. No ensemble was evaluated on this already-used panel.
Public history sensitivity

For evenly spaced saved development decisions, the public 409-value observation was held fixed and direct policy predictions compared actual history against empty history. This ran no environment transitions or optimizer steps. Empty history can be out of distribution; action sensitivity is not causal feature importance or evidence that removing history improves or harms navigation.
Uncertainty and failure evidence

A descriptive 2,000-replicate family-cluster bootstrap uses eight development/demo families. The ensemble-minus-Q-learning success-difference interval spans 0 to about 0.201. Differences against the three perfect individual policies are zero throughout the observed panel; those degenerate intervals do not prove zero uncertainty on new populations. There is one training seed and no new held-out ensemble assessment. Q-learning and the observed-map planner each timed out twice; Random collided on all 36 cases. All failures and vote traces remain in the export.
